    88	theorem avg_wrong_ordered_norm_sq_le (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
    89	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z)
    90	    (r t : F) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    91	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v =>
    92	      ‖applyOperatorToState ((1 - X.effect r) *
    93	        orderedIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤
    94	      2 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
    95	  classical
    96	  let w (bc : F × F) := stateQForm ψ
    97	    (Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2)
    98	  have hw (bc : F × F) : 0 ≤ w bc :=
    99	    stateQForm_nonneg ψ ((pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement X Z hZ).1 bc)
   100	  have hsum : ∑ bc, w bc = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   101	    rw [← stateQForm_one ψ, ← (pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement X Z hZ).2,
   102	      stateQForm_finset_sum]
   103	    rfl
   104	  have hpoint (v : Fin 2 → F) :
   105	      ‖applyOperatorToState ((1 - X.effect r) *
   106	        orderedIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   107	      (if v 1 = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0) + ∑ bc : F × F,
   108	        (if v 0 * bc.1 + v 1 * bc.2 = v 0 * r + v 1 * t ∧ bc.1 ≠ r
   109	          then 1 else 0) * w bc := by
   110	    by_cases hv : v 1 = 0
   111	    · rw [if_pos hv]
   112	      apply le_trans (b := ‖ψ‖ ^ 2)
   113	      · apply pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _)
   114	        rw [applyOperatorToState_mul]
   115	        exact (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le
   116	          (MagicSquareRigidity.conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (hX r).one_sub) _).trans
   117	          (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le
   118	            (orderedIndicator_gram_le_one X Z hX hZ _ _ _) ψ)
   119	      · exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (Finset.sum_nonneg fun bc _ =>
   120	          mul_nonneg (by split_ifs <;> norm_num) (hw bc))
   121	    · rw [if_neg hv, zero_add, MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq]
   122	      change stateQForm ψ _ ≤ _
   123	      rw [wrong_ordered_gram X Z hX r _ _ _ hv, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   124	      apply le_of_eq
   125	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   126	      intro bc _
   127	      split_ifs <;> simp [w, stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]

   129	      (fun v => if v 1 = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0) =

   133	    rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (finTwoArrowEquiv F)]
   134	    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   135	    rw [avgOver_uniform_snd (fun β : F => if β = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0)]
   136	    simp [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
   137	  have hcollision (bc : F × F) :

   141	    by_cases hb : bc.1 = r
   142	    · simp [hb, avgOver_uniform_const]
   143	    · rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (finTwoArrowEquiv F)]
   144	      have h := affine_collision_average bc (r, t)
   145	      have hne : bc ≠ (r, t) := fun h => hb (congrArg Prod.fst h)
   146	      simpa [finTwoArrowEquiv, hb, hne] using h.le
   147	  have h := avgOver_mono (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) _ _ hpoint
   148	  simp only [avgOver_add, avgOver_sum, avgOver_mul_const, hexc] at h
   149	  refine h.trans ?_
   150	  have hc := Finset.sum_le_sum (s := Finset.univ) fun bc _ =>
   151	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hcollision bc) (hw bc)
   152	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hsum] at hc

   155	/-- Point mismatch on a retained polynomial is at most twice its ordered
   156	residual plus `4/q` times its unnormalized mass. Reverse the point order to

   159	theorem point_mismatch_le_ordered_error (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   160	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z)
   161	    (r t : F) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   162	    ‖applyOperatorToState (1 - X.effect r) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤

   165	          (orderedIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) ψ‖ ^ 2) +
   166	      4 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by

   168	      ‖applyOperatorToState (1 - X.effect r) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤

   172	          orderedIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by

     4	/-!
     5	# Common exceptional fibers for polynomial coefficients
     6	
     7	A nonconstant polynomial in one block, with polynomial coefficients in a
     8	second block, has a nonzero coefficient at a nonconstant monomial. Its zero set controls
     9	all exceptional specializations simultaneously, independently of the outcome
    10	of a measurement. The weights may depend on the fixed block but not on the
    11	block being averaged.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1341-1358`,
    16	especially `eq:qld-g-2`; support for blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolynomialImageBounds
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F]
    29	
    30	private theorem exists_nonconstant_coeff {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ}
    31	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (hp : ¬ ∃ r, p = MvPolynomial.C r) :
    32	    ∃ e : Fin n →₀ ℕ, e ≠ 0 ∧ p.coeff e ≠ 0 := by
    33	  classical
    34	  by_contra! h
    35	  apply hp
    36	  refine ⟨p.coeff 0, ?_⟩
    37	  ext e
    38	  by_cases he : e = 0
    39	  · simp [he]
    40	  · simp [MvPolynomial.coeff_C, Ne.symm he, h e he]
    41	
    42	/-- A single coefficient defines the exceptional slices for every field
    43	outcome. Outside its zero set, every fiber has probability at most `D/q`;
    44	the exceptional set itself has probability at most `C/q`. Both degree
    45	conditions concern the displayed polynomial, not an assumed collision law.
    46	This is the common-set argument following `eq:qld-g-2`, supporting
    47	blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    48	theorem exists_common_exceptional_coefficient {n k C D : ℕ}
    49	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin k) F))
    50	    (hp : ¬ ∃ r, p = MvPolynomial.C r)
    51	    (hcoeff : ∀ e, (p.coeff e).totalDegree ≤ C) (hdegree : p.totalDegree ≤ D) :
    52	    ∃ e : Fin n →₀ ℕ, e ≠ 0 ∧ p.coeff e ≠ 0 ∧
    53	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F))
    54	        (fun z => if MvPolynomial.eval z (p.coeff e) = 0 then 1 else 0) ≤
    55	          (C : ℝ) / Fintype.card F ∧
    56	      ∀ z : Fin k → F, MvPolynomial.eval z (p.coeff e) ≠ 0 → ∀ b : F,
    57	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F))
    58	          (fun x => if MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p) = b
    59	            then 1 else 0) ≤ (D : ℝ) / Fintype.card F := by
    60	  obtain ⟨e, he, hc⟩ := exists_nonconstant_coeff p hp
    61	  refine ⟨e, he, hc, ?_, ?_⟩
    62	  · simpa using avg_eval_eq_le (p.coeff e) 0 hc (hcoeff e) (by simp)
    63	  · intro z hz b
    64	    have hne : MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p ≠ MvPolynomial.C b := by
    65	      intro h
    66	      apply hz
    67	      have h' := congrArg (MvPolynomial.coeff e) h
    68	      simpa [MvPolynomial.coeff_map, MvPolynomial.coeff_C, Ne.symm he] using h'
    69	    have hd : (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p).totalDegree ≤ D :=
    70	      (Finset.sup_mono (MvPolynomial.support_map_subset _ _)).trans hdegree
    71	    simpa using avg_eval_eq_le _ (MvPolynomial.C b) hne hd (by simp)
    72	
    73	/-- Summing all nonnegative outcome weights before averaging exceptional
    74	slices avoids an outcome-cardinality factor. The weights may depend on `z`
    75	and their sum is the same mass `M` at every `z`. This is the weighted fiber
    76	calculation in `eq:qld-g-2`, supporting blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    77	theorem avg_weighted_fiber_le {n k C D : ℕ}
    78	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin k) F))
    79	    (hp : ¬ ∃ r, p = MvPolynomial.C r)
    80	    (hcoeff : ∀ e, (p.coeff e).totalDegree ≤ C) (hdegree : p.totalDegree ≤ D)
    81	    (w : (Fin k → F) → F → ℝ) (M : ℝ)
    82	    (hw : ∀ z b, 0 ≤ w z b) (hsum : ∀ z, ∑ b, w z b = M) :
    83	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F)) (fun z => ∑ b : F,
    84	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F))
    85	        (fun x => if MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p) = b
    86	          then 1 else 0) * w z b) ≤ ((C + D : ℕ) : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * M := by
    87	  classical
    88	  obtain ⟨e, _, _, hbad, hgood⟩ :=
    89	    exists_common_exceptional_coefficient p hp hcoeff hdegree
    90	  have hM : 0 ≤ M := by
    91	    rw [← hsum (fun _ => 0)]
    92	    exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => hw _ b
    93	  have hpoint (z : Fin k → F) :
    94	      (∑ b : F, avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F))
    95	        (fun x => if MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p) = b
    96	          then 1 else 0) * w z b) ≤
    97	      (if MvPolynomial.eval z (p.coeff e) = 0 then 1 else 0) * M +
    98	        (D : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * M := by
    99	    by_cases hz : MvPolynomial.eval z (p.coeff e) = 0
   100	    · simp only [hz, if_true, one_mul]
   101	      apply le_trans (b := M)
   102	      · rw [← hsum z]
   103	        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   104	        intro b _
   105	        apply le_trans (b := 1 * w z b)
   106	        · apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ (hw z b)
   107	          apply avgOver_uniform_le_const
   108	          intro x
   109	          split_ifs <;> norm_num
   110	        · rw [one_mul]
   111	      · exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (mul_nonneg (by positivity) hM)
   112	    · simp only [hz, if_false, zero_mul, zero_add]
   113	      rw [← hsum z, Finset.mul_sum]
   114	      exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ =>
   115	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hgood z hz b) (hw z b)
   116	  calc
   117	    _ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F)) (fun z =>
   118	        (if MvPolynomial.eval z (p.coeff e) = 0 then 1 else 0) * M +
   119	          (D : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * M) := avgOver_mono _ _ _ hpoint
   120	    _ ≤ (C : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * M + (D : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * M := by
   121	      rw [avgOver_add, avgOver_mul_const, avgOver_uniform_const]
   122	      exact add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbad hM) le_rfl
   123	    _ = _ := by push_cast; ring

   127	private theorem avg_diagonalIndicator_linear_le
   128	    (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι) (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z)
   129	    (r t : F) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   130	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v =>
   131	      stateQForm ψ (diagonalIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t))) ≤
   132	      (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   133	        stateQForm ψ (Z.effect t * X.effect r * Z.effect t) := by
   134	  classical
   135	  let w (bc : F × F) : ℝ := stateQForm ψ
   136	    (Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2)
   137	  have hw (bc : F × F) : 0 ≤ w bc :=
   138	    stateQForm_nonneg ψ ((pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement X Z hZ).1 bc)
   139	  have hsum : ∑ bc, w bc = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   140	    rw [← stateQForm_one ψ, ← (pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement X Z hZ).2,
   141	      stateQForm_finset_sum]
   142	    rfl
   143	  have hexpand (v : Fin 2 → F) :
   144	      stateQForm ψ (diagonalIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) =
   145	      ∑ bc : F × F, (if v 0 * bc.1 + v 1 * bc.2 = v 0 * r + v 1 * t
   146	        then 1 else 0) * w bc := by
   147	    rw [diagonalIndicator, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   148	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   149	    intro bc _
   150	    split_ifs <;> simp [w, stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
   151	  have hcollision (bc : F × F) :
   152	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v =>
   153	        if v 0 * bc.1 + v 1 * bc.2 = v 0 * r + v 1 * t then (1 : ℝ) else 0) =
   154	        if bc = (r, t) then 1 else (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
   155	    rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (finTwoArrowEquiv F)]
   156	    exact affine_collision_average bc (r, t)
   157	  simp_rw [hexpand, avgOver_sum, avgOver_mul_const, hcollision]
   158	  calc
   159	    _ ≤ ∑ bc : F × F, ((Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ +
   160	        if bc = (r, t) then 1 else 0) * w bc := by
   161	      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   162	      intro bc _
   163	      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ (hw bc)
   164	      split_ifs <;> simp
   165	    _ = _ := by
   166	      simp_rw [add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   167	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hsum]
   168	      simp [w]

   170	private theorem avg_orderedIndicator_linear_le
   171	    (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι) (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X)
   172	    (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z) (r t : F) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   173	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v =>
   174	      ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator X Z (v 0) (v 1)
   175	        (v 0 * r + v 1 * t)) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤
   176	      2 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 + stateQForm ψ (Z.effect t) := by
   177	  have hexc : avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F))
   178	      (fun v => if v 1 = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0) =
   179	        (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   180	    change avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F))
   181	      (fun v => if ((finTwoArrowEquiv F) v).2 = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0) = _
   182	    rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (finTwoArrowEquiv F)]
   183	    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   184	    rw [avgOver_uniform_snd (fun β : F => if β = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0)]
   185	    simp [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
   186	  have hdrop : stateQForm ψ (Z.effect t * X.effect r * Z.effect t) ≤
   187	      stateQForm ψ (Z.effect t) := by
   188	    apply quadratic_form_mono
   189	    simpa only [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, measurement_effect_hermitian, mul_one,
   190	      (hZ t).isIdempotentElem.eq] using
   191	      star_left_conjugate_le_conjugate (measurement_effect_le_one X r) (Z.effect t)
   192	  have havg := avgOver_mono (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) _ _ (fun v =>
   193	    le_trans (le_abs_self _) (abs_orderedIndicator_norm_sq_sub_diagonal_le
   194	      X Z hX hZ (v 0) (v 1) (v 0 * r + v 1 * t) ψ))
   195	  rw [avgOver_sub, hexc] at havg
   196	  have hdiag := avg_diagonalIndicator_linear_le X Z hZ r t ψ
   197	  linarith
   198	
   199	/-- The wrong-variable coefficient is concentrated only after the middle
   200	contraction has been removed. The outer measurement depends solely on the
   201	fixed block `z`; `X` depends solely on the varying block `x`. For the other
   202	class interchange `X,Z` and the two blocks. The vector is arbitrary and
   203	need not be normalized. This proves the local norm bound behind
   204	`eq:qld-g-prime-xpt-bound` and its reversed-order counterpart, supporting
   205	blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
   206	theorem avg_orderedIndicator_norm_sq_le_of_nonconstant {n k C D : ℕ}
   207	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin k) F))
   208	    (hp : ¬ ∃ r, p = MvPolynomial.C r)
   209	    (hcoeff : ∀ e, (p.coeff e).totalDegree ≤ C) (hdegree : p.totalDegree ≤ D)
   210	    (r : (Fin n → F) → (Fin k → F) → F)
   211	    (X : (Fin n → F) → Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   212	    (Z : (Fin k → F) → Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   213	    (hX : ∀ x, Measurement.IsProjective (X x))
   214	    (hZ : ∀ z, Measurement.IsProjective (Z z)) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   215	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F)) (fun z =>
   216	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F)) (fun x =>
   217	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v =>
   218	          ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator (X x) (Z z) (v 0) (v 1)
   219	            (v 0 * r x z + v 1 *
   220	              MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p))) ψ‖ ^ 2))) ≤
   221	      ((C + D + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   222	  classical
   223	  let w (z : Fin k → F) (b : F) := stateQForm ψ ((Z z).effect b)
   224	  have hsum (z : Fin k → F) : ∑ b, w z b = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   225	    rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, (Z z).sum_eq_one, stateQForm_one]
   226	  have hfiber := avg_weighted_fiber_le p hp hcoeff hdegree w (‖ψ‖ ^ 2)
   227	    (fun z b => stateQForm_nonneg ψ ((Z z).pos b)) hsum
   228	  have heval (z : Fin k → F) (x : Fin n → F) :
   229	      stateQForm ψ ((Z z).effect
   230	        (MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p))) =
   231	      ∑ b : F, (if MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p) = b
   232	        then 1 else 0) * w z b := by
   233	    simp [w]
   234	  calc
   235	    _ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F)) (fun z =>
   236	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F)) (fun x =>
   237	          2 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   238	          stateQForm ψ ((Z z).effect
   239	            (MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p))))) := by
   240	      apply avgOver_mono
   241	      intro z
   242	      apply avgOver_mono
   243	      intro x
   244	      exact avg_orderedIndicator_linear_le (X x) (Z z) (hX x) (hZ z) _ _ ψ
   245	    _ = 2 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   246	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin k → F)) (fun z => ∑ b : F,
   247	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F))
   248	            (fun x => if MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval z) p) = b
   249	              then 1 else 0) * w z b) := by
   250	      simp_rw [heval, avgOver_add, avgOver_uniform_const, avgOver_sum, avgOver_mul_const]
   251	    _ ≤ 2 * (Fintype.card F : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   252	        ((C + D : ℕ) : ℝ) / Fintype.card F * ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := add_le_add le_rfl hfiber
   253	    _ = _ := by push_cast; ring
   254

     5	/-!
     6	# Indicator-weighted ordered projectors
     7	
     8	This module proves the local norm calculation in `eq:qld-g-prime`. The state
     9	vector is not assumed normalized: its squared norm controls the exceptional
    10	coefficient, so the estimate can be summed over all polynomial outcomes.
    11	The measurements act on an arbitrary finite space, which includes either
    12	player's placed expanded measurements.
    13	
    14	The coefficient-polynomial argument also bounds mass outside the scalar-linear
    15	image, with its actual ordered-correlation error displayed in the conclusion.
    16	These are auxiliary estimates, not the global polynomial-pair construction.
    17	The remaining block-separation and construction obligations are recorded in
    18	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex` and issue #513.
    19	
    20	Only the dependency chain needed for these estimates is exposed; supporting
    21	lemmas remain private.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	* `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1289-1326`,
    26	  especially `eq:qld-g-42`, `eq:qld-g-43`, and `eq:qld-g-prime`.
    27	-/

    43	/-- The ordered product selected by the linear field-answer check in
    44	`eq:qld-g-42`. This is an operator, not an asserted measurement effect. -/
    45	def orderedIndicator (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι) (α β a : F) : Op ι :=
    46	  ∑ bc : F × F, if α * bc.1 + β * bc.2 = a then X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The diagonal sandwich sum in `eq:qld-g-prime`. -/
    49	def diagonalIndicator (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι) (α β a : F) : Op ι :=
    50	  ∑ bc : F × F,
    51	    if α * bc.1 + β * bc.2 = a then
    52	      Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2 else 0
    53	
    54	/-- For a nonzero second coefficient, X orthogonality and cancellation in
    55	the field eliminate every off-diagonal term of the ordered Gram operator.
    56	This is the exact local algebra behind `eq:qld-g-prime`; no commutation of
    57	the X and Z measurements is assumed. -/
    58	private theorem orderedIndicator_gram_of_ne_zero (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
    59	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (α β a : F) (hβ : β ≠ 0) :
    60	    (orderedIndicator X Z α β a)ᴴ * orderedIndicator X Z α β a =
    61	      diagonalIndicator X Z α β a := by
    62	  classical
    63	  unfold orderedIndicator diagonalIndicator
    64	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    65	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun bc _ => ?_
    66	  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single bc]
    67	  · by_cases h : α * bc.1 + β * bc.2 = a
    68	    · simp only [if_pos h, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, measurement_effect_hermitian]
    69	      rw [mul_assoc (Z.effect bc.2), ← mul_assoc (X.effect bc.1),
    70	        (hX bc.1).isIdempotentElem.eq, ← mul_assoc]
    71	    · simp [h]
    72	  · intro bc' _ hne
    73	    by_cases h : α * bc.1 + β * bc.2 = a
    74	    · by_cases h' : α * bc'.1 + β * bc'.2 = a
    75	      · have hb : bc.1 ≠ bc'.1 := by
    76	          intro hb
    77	          have hc : bc.2 = bc'.2 := mul_left_cancel₀ hβ (by
    78	            apply add_left_cancel (a := α * bc.1)
    79	            simpa only [hb] using h.trans h'.symm)
    80	          exact hne (Prod.ext hb hc).symm
    81	        simp only [if_pos h, if_pos h', Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
    82	          measurement_effect_hermitian]
    83	        calc
    84	          Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * (X.effect bc'.1 * Z.effect bc'.2) =
    85	              Z.effect bc.2 * (X.effect bc.1 * X.effect bc'.1) * Z.effect bc'.2 := by
    86	            simp only [mul_assoc]
    87	          _ = 0 := by rw [projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero X hX hb]; simp
    88	      · simp [h']
    89	    · simp [h]
    90	  · simp

    92	/-- The squared state norm of the ordered indicator equals its diagonal
    93	sandwich quadratic form when the second coefficient is nonzero. -/
    94	private theorem orderedIndicator_norm_sq_of_ne_zero (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
    95	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (α β a : F) (hβ : β ≠ 0)
    96	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    97	    ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator X Z α β a) ψ‖ ^ 2 =
    98	      stateQForm ψ (diagonalIndicator X Z α β a) := by
    99	  rw [MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq,
   100	    orderedIndicator_gram_of_ne_zero X Z hX α β a hβ]
   101	  rfl

   103	/-- The diagonal indicator is a positive contraction, since it selects
   104	effects from the complete sandwich POVM. -/
   105	private theorem diagonalIndicator_bounds (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   106	    (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z) (α β a : F) :
   107	    0 ≤ diagonalIndicator X Z α β a ∧ diagonalIndicator X Z α β a ≤ 1 := by
   108	  obtain ⟨hpos, hsum⟩ := pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement X Z hZ
   109	  change (∀ bc : F × F, 0 ≤ Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2) at hpos
   110	  change (∑ bc : F × F, Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2) = 1 at hsum
   111	  constructor
   112	  · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun bc _ => by
   113	      split_ifs
   114	      · exact hpos bc
   115	      · exact le_refl 0
   116	  · calc
   117	      diagonalIndicator X Z α β a ≤
   118	          ∑ bc : F × F, Z.effect bc.2 * X.effect bc.1 * Z.effect bc.2 := by
   119	        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun bc _ => ?_
   120	        split_ifs
   121	        · exact le_refl _
   122	        · exact hpos bc
   123	      _ = 1 := hsum

   125	/-- At the exceptional coefficient zero, completeness of Z leaves a
   126	coarse-grained X projection. This includes zero first coefficient. -/
   127	private theorem orderedIndicator_zero (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι) (α a : F) :
   128	    orderedIndicator X Z α 0 a = (X.postprocess (fun b => α * b)).effect a := by
   129	  unfold orderedIndicator
   130	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
   131	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   132	  by_cases h : α * b = a
   133	  · simp only [zero_mul, add_zero, h, if_true]
   134	    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Z.sum_eq_one, mul_one]
   135	  · simp [h]

   137	/-- Every linear-answer ordered indicator is a contraction. For nonzero
   138	second coefficient this follows from the diagonal identity; at zero it
   139	follows from completeness and projective postprocessing. -/
   140	theorem orderedIndicator_gram_le_one (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   141	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z) (α β a : F) :
   142	    (orderedIndicator X Z α β a)ᴴ * orderedIndicator X Z α β a ≤ 1 := by
   143	  by_cases hβ : β = 0
   144	  · subst β
   145	    rw [orderedIndicator_zero, measurement_effect_hermitian,
   146	      (SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective X hX (fun b => α * b) a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   147	    exact measurement_effect_le_one _ _
   148	  · rw [orderedIndicator_gram_of_ne_zero X Z hX α β a hβ]
   149	    exact (diagonalIndicator_bounds X Z hZ α β a).2

   151	/-- The pointwise error in `eq:qld-g-prime` is supported on the zero second
   152	coefficient and bounded by the squared norm of the actual state vector. -/
   153	theorem abs_orderedIndicator_norm_sq_sub_diagonal_le (X Z : Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   154	    (hX : Measurement.IsProjective X) (hZ : Measurement.IsProjective Z)
   155	    (α β a : F) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   156	    |‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator X Z α β a) ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   157	        stateQForm ψ (diagonalIndicator X Z α β a)| ≤
   158	      if β = 0 then ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0 := by
   159	  by_cases hβ : β = 0
   160	  · rw [if_pos hβ]
   161	    have hA0 := sq_nonneg ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator X Z α β a) ψ‖
   162	    have hA1 : ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator X Z α β a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   163	      rw [MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, ← stateQForm_one ψ]
   164	      exact quadratic_form_mono (orderedIndicator_gram_le_one X Z hX hZ α β a) ψ
   165	    have hD := diagonalIndicator_bounds X Z hZ α β a
   166	    have hD0 := stateQForm_nonneg ψ hD.1
   167	    have hD1 : stateQForm ψ (diagonalIndicator X Z α β a) ≤ ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   168	      rw [← stateQForm_one ψ]
   169	      exact quadratic_form_mono hD.2 ψ
   170	    exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩
   171	  · rw [if_neg hβ, orderedIndicator_norm_sq_of_ne_zero X Z hX α β a hβ ψ]
   172	    simp

   174	/-- Completeness and projectivity preserve total squared state mass. This is
   175	the normalization used after summing `eq:qld-g-prime` over polynomial labels. -/
   176	theorem sum_projective_state_norm_sq {Γ : Type*} [Fintype Γ]
   177	    (S : Quantum.Measurement Γ ι) (hS : Measurement.IsProjective S)
   178	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   179	    ∑ g : Γ, ‖applyOperatorToState (S.effect g) ψ‖ ^ 2 = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   180	  simp_rw [MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, measurement_effect_hermitian,
   181	    fun g => (hS g).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   182	  change (∑ g : Γ, stateQForm ψ (S.effect g)) = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2
   183	  rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, S.sum_eq_one, stateQForm_one]
   184	
   185	/-- A polynomial not of the form `alpha * u + beta * v` has a nonzero
   186	coefficient outside those two monomials. Applied over the ring of base-point
   187	polynomials, this chooses one coefficient independently of both measurement
   188	outcomes in the argument following `eq:qld-g-prime`. -/
   189	private theorem exists_nonzero_nonlinear_coeff {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
   190	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R)
   191	    (hp : ¬ ∃ u v : R, p = MvPolynomial.C u * MvPolynomial.X 0 +
   192	      MvPolynomial.C v * MvPolynomial.X 1) :

   392	/-- The ordered polynomial estimate sums over any specified set of polynomial
   393	labels outside the scalar-linear image. Each label is weighted by its actual
   394	state mass; the estimate never replaces a sum by the number of labels. -/
   395	private theorem avg_sum_orderedIndicator_norm_sq_le_of_not_linear {n : ℕ} {Γ : Type*}
   396	    (s : Finset Γ) (p : Γ → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) F))
   397	    (hp : ∀ g ∈ s, ¬ ∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F,
   398	      p g = MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 + MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1)
   399	    (X Z : (Fin n → F) → Quantum.Measurement F ι)
   400	    (hX : ∀ u, Measurement.IsProjective (X u))
   401	    (hZ : ∀ u, Measurement.IsProjective (Z u)) (ψ : Γ → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   402	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F)) (fun u =>
   403	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v => ∑ g ∈ s,
   404	        ‖applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator (X u) (Z u) (v 0) (v 1)

   406	      ∑ g ∈ s,
   407	        (((p g).support.sup fun e => ((p g).coeff e).totalDegree) +
   408	          max 1 (p g).totalDegree + 1 : ℕ) / (Fintype.card F : ℝ) * ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 := by

   425	  rw [sub_add_cancel] at htriangle
   426	  have hsquare := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) htriangle 2

   439	    (hZ : ∀ u, Measurement.IsProjective (Z u)) (ψ : Γ → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   440	    ∑ g ∈ s, ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 ≤
   441	      2 * avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F)) (fun u =>
   442	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → F)) (fun v => ∑ g ∈ s,
   443	          ‖ψ g - applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator (X u) (Z u) (v 0) (v 1)
   444	            (MvPolynomial.eval v (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval u) (p g)))) (ψ g)‖ ^ 2)) +

   455	  have havg := avgOver_mono (uniformDistribution (Fin n → F)) _ _ fun u =>

   461	      (fun v => ∑ g ∈ s, ‖ψ g - A u v g‖ ^ 2)) + _

   464	      (fun v => ∑ g ∈ s, ‖A u v g‖ ^ 2)) ≤ _ at hnorm

     6	
     7	The singleton polynomial is transported through the canonical field equivalence
     8	and Mathlib's equivalence between a polynomial in a sum of variables and an
     9	iterated polynomial ring. Its individual-degree certificate controls both levels.
    10	Splitting each base coefficient by either block gives the partial degrees used
    11	in the fiber calculation. Independence of both wrong blocks identifies the
    12	outcome with the existing bounded polynomial-pair combining map.

    34	    ((MvPolynomial.sumRingEquiv F A B p).coeff a).coeff b =
    35	      p.coeff (Finsupp.sumFinsuppAddEquivProdFinsupp.symm (a, b)) := by

    39	private theorem totalDegree_le_of_exponents {F : Type*} [CommSemiring F]

   382	outcome in the existing bounded `combinePoly` image. The two components have
   383	individual degree at most `d`, not merely total degree at most `md`.
   384	This identifies the separated image in `eq:qld-g-non-separable` with
   385	`def:combine-map`, supporting blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
   386	theorem exists_polyPair_of_scalar_separated (P : AdmissibleParams)
   387	    (g : DirectPolyTuple P.extendedDirectLd)
   388	    (hlin : ∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m)) (PauliScalar P),
   389	      scalarPolynomial P g = MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 +
   390	        MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1)
   391	    (hX : ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g (Finsupp.single 0 1) true = MvPolynomial.C r)
   392	    (hZ : ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g (Finsupp.single 1 1) false = MvPolynomial.C r) :
   393	    ∃ pair : PolyPair P,
   394	      MvPolynomial.map (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).toRingHom (g (0 : Fin 1)).1 =
   395	        combinePoly pair.1.1 pair.2.1 := by
   396	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := blockCoefficientPolynomial_const g _ true hX
   397	  obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := blockCoefficientPolynomial_const g _ false hZ
   398	  refine ⟨(f, h), ?_⟩
   399	  apply MvPolynomial.rename_injective (scalarBaseCoordinateEquiv P.m)
   400	    (scalarBaseCoordinateEquiv P.m).injective
   401	  apply (MvPolynomial.sumRingEquiv (PauliScalar P) (Fin 2) (Fin (2 * P.m))).injective
   402	  change scalarPolynomial P g = _
   403	  rw [scalarExpansion_combinePoly]
   404	  obtain ⟨r, t, hlin⟩ := hlin
   405	  have h01 : (Finsupp.single (0 : Fin 2) 1 : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ) ≠ Finsupp.single 1 1 := by
   406	    intro h
   407	    simpa using congrArg (fun e : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ => e 0) h
   408	  simp only [hlin, MvPolynomial.coeff_add, MvPolynomial.coeff_C_mul,
   409	    MvPolynomial.coeff_X, h01, Ne.symm h01, ↓reduceIte, mul_one, mul_zero,
   410	    add_zero, zero_add] at hf hh
   411	  change r = MvPolynomial.rename (fun i => (baseCoordinateEquiv P.m).symm (.inl i)) f.1 at hf
   412	  change t = MvPolynomial.rename (fun i => (baseCoordinateEquiv P.m).symm (.inr i)) h.1 at hh
   413	  rw [hlin, hf, hh]
   414	
   415	end ExtendedLineGame

     4	/-!
     5	# Scalar-nonlinear mass of the actual rounded measurements
     6	
     7	The full polynomial-outcome ordered estimate is composed with the concentration
     8	bound for scalar-nonlinear outcomes. Opposite placements commute; no symmetry of the
     9	player spaces is required. Projectivity retains the actual outcome masses.

    12	
    13	`eq:qld-g-42`, `eq:qld-g-prime`, and `eq:qld-g-prime-bound`, paper
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1283-1326`.
    15	This is only scalar-linearity concentration; the variable-separation estimates
    16	and retained overlaps are separate results.
    17	-/

    30	/-- Actual mass of outcomes outside `alpha*g1(x,z) + beta*g2(x,z)`. The
    31	coefficients may still depend on both base blocks. -/
    32	def scalarNonlinearMass {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    33	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
    34	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) : ℝ := by
    35	  classical
    36	  exact ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g => ¬ ∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m))
    37	      (PauliScalar P), scalarPolynomial P g =
    38	        MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 + MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1),
    39	    ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2
    40	
    41	private theorem placed_orderedIndicator {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    42	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) (x : ExtendedPointQuestion P)
    43	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    44	    orderedIndicator (S.placedMeasurement p (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X x.1.1))
    45	      (S.placedMeasurement p (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z x.1.2)) x.2.1 x.2.2 a =
    46	    S.place p (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
    47	        x.2.1 * ab.1 + x.2.2 * ab.2 = a),
    48	      (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X x.1.1).effect ab.1 *
    49	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z x.1.2).effect ab.2) := by
    50	  rw [S.place_finsetSum, Finset.sum_filter]
    51	  simp only [orderedIndicator, ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect,
    52	    ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]
    53	
    54	/-- Opposite placements commute, identifying the residual on the actual
    55	projected state with the ordered-error residual. This supports both orders
    56	of `eq:qld-g-42/43` and blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    57	theorem placed_residual {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    58	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopposite : p1.IsOpposite p2)
    59	    (R : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side)) (T : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p2.side)) :
    60	    applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 R) S.psiHat -
    61	      applyOperatorToState (S.place p2 T)
    62	        (applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 R) S.psiHat) =
    63	      applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 R * (1 - S.place p2 T)) S.psiHat := by
    64	  rw [← applyOperatorToState_mul, ← S.place_comm p1 p2 hopposite R T, mul_sub, mul_one]
    65	  simp only [applyOperatorToState, map_sub, LinearMap.sub_apply]
    66	
    67	/-- The scalar-nonlinear outcome mass is bounded by twice the actual full
    68	ordered error plus `2*((2m+2)d+1)/q`. All transports and degree bounds are
    69	derived internally from the actual singleton outcomes. This auxiliary applies
    70	to every opposite placement of a complete projective measurement. -/
    71	theorem scalarNonlinearMass_le_ordered_error {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    72	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopposite : p1.IsOpposite p2)
    73	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side))
    74	    (hR : Measurement.IsProjective R) :
    75	    scalarNonlinearMass S p1 R ≤ 2 * extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R false +
    76	      2 * (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q := by
    77	  classical
    78	  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun g => ¬ ∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m))
    79	      (PauliScalar P), scalarPolynomial P g =
    80	        MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 + MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1)
    81	  let ψ := fun g => applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 (R.effect g)) S.psiHat
    82	  let X := fun u : Fin (2 * P.m) → PauliScalar P => S.placedMeasurement p2
    83	    (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X (fun i => u ((baseCoordinateEquiv P.m).symm (.inl i))))
    84	  let Z := fun u : Fin (2 * P.m) → PauliScalar P => S.placedMeasurement p2
    85	    (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z (fun i => u ((baseCoordinateEquiv P.m).symm (.inr i))))
    86	  have hX : ∀ u, Measurement.IsProjective (X u) := fun u =>
    87	    S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p2 _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _)
    88	  have hZ : ∀ u, Measurement.IsProjective (Z u) := fun u =>
    89	    S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p2 _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _)
    90	  have h := nonlinear_mass_le_ordered_error s (scalarPolynomial P)
    91	    (fun g hg => (Finset.mem_filter.mp hg).2) X Z hX hZ ψ
    92	  have hmass : ∑ g, ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
    93	    simpa only [ψ, ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect, S.psiHat_norm, one_pow] using
    94	      sum_projective_state_norm_sq (S.placedMeasurement p1 R)
    95	        (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p1 R hR) S.psiHat
    96	  have hdegree : (∑ g ∈ s,
    97	      (((scalarPolynomial P g).support.sup fun e =>
    98	          ((scalarPolynomial P g).coeff e).totalDegree) +
    99	        max 1 (scalarPolynomial P g).totalDegree + 1 : ℕ) /
   100	          (Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) * ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2) ≤
   101	      (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q := by
   102	    have hcard : Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) = P.q :=
   103	      @FieldModel.card P.q P.model.toFieldModel
   104	    rw [hcard]
   105	    calc
   106	      _ ≤ ∑ g ∈ s, ((((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) * ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 := by
   107	        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   108	        intro g _
   109	        apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ (sq_nonneg _)
   110	        apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
   111	        exact_mod_cast scalarPolynomial_degree_term_le P g
   112	      _ ≤ ∑ g, ((((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) * ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 :=
   113	        Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _) (by
   114	          intros; positivity)
   115	      _ = _ := by rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hmass, mul_one]
   116	  let f := fun (u : Fin (2 * P.m) → PauliScalar P) (v : Fin 2 → PauliScalar P) g =>
   117	    ‖ψ g - applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator (X u) (Z u) (v 0) (v 1)
   118	      (MvPolynomial.eval v (MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval u)
   119	        (scalarPolynomial P g)))) (ψ g)‖ ^ 2
   120	  have hfull : avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m) → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   121	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → PauliScalar P)) (fun v => ∑ g, f u v g)) =
   122	        extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R false := by
   123	    rw [← avgOver_uniform_prod (fun u v => ∑ g, f u v g)]
   124	    unfold extendedPolynomialOrderedError
   125	    rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P).symm]
   126	    apply avgOver_congr
   127	    rintro ⟨u, v⟩
   128	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   129	    intro g _
   130	    dsimp only [f]
   131	    rw [scalarPolynomial_eval]
   132	    have hXZ : orderedIndicator (X u) (Z u) (v 0) (v 1)
   133	        (extendedPolynomialRead P (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)) g) =
   134	        orderedIndicator
   135	          (S.placedMeasurement p2 (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X
   136	            (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)).1.1))
   137	          (S.placedMeasurement p2 (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z
   138	            (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)).1.2))
   139	          (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)).2.1
   140	          (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)).2.2
   141	          (extendedPolynomialRead P (scalarBaseQuestionEquiv P (u, v)) g) := by
   142	      simp [X, Z, scalarBaseQuestionEquiv, Equiv.piCongrLeft_apply]
   143	    rw [hXZ, placed_orderedIndicator]
   144	    dsimp only [ψ]
   145	    rw [placed_residual S p1 p2 hopposite]
   146	    rfl
   147	  have herror : avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m) → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   148	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin 2 → PauliScalar P)) (fun v => ∑ g ∈ s, f u v g)) ≤
   149	        extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R false := by
   150	    rw [← hfull]
   151	    apply avgOver_mono
   152	    intro u
   153	    apply avgOver_mono
   154	    intro v
   155	    exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _) (by
   156	      intros; exact sq_nonneg _)
   157	  change scalarNonlinearMass S p1 R ≤ 2 * _ + 2 * _ at h
   158	  have hout := h.trans (add_le_add
   159	    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left herror (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2))
   160	    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdegree (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)))
   161	  simpa only [mul_div_assoc] using hout
   162	
   163	/-- Actual rounded measurements satisfy scalar-linearity concentration for both
   164	player placements, with all point, line, soundness, and rounding errors retained.
   165	The measurements are produced by `exists_rounded_polynomial_ordered_estimates`;
   166	neither an ordered estimate nor a mass bound is an assumption. Both ordered
   167	estimates remain available for the subsequent variable-separation argument.
   168	
   169	The directly indexed, completed-answer line witness is an explicit restriction
   170	of this auxiliary, as documented in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
   171	and `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex`. This proves only the
   172	scalar-linearity calculation `eq:qld-g-prime-bound`, not `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
   173	theorem exists_rounded_polynomial_scalar_mass :
   174	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   175	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε δQ δL : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   176	        (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ) (_lines : ExtendedLinesWitness S points δL),
   177	      let delta := deltaLd a b
   178	        (directPassingErrorEnvelope (δQ + δL) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q))
   179	        P.q (2 * P.m + 2) P.d 1
   180	      let eta := delta + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow delta (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
   181	        2 * Real.sqrt (2 * delta)
   182	      ∃ RA : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice),
   183	      ∃ RB : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob),
   184	        Measurement.IsProjective RA ∧ Measurement.IsProjective RB ∧
   185	        (∀ reverse : Bool,
   186	          extendedPolynomialOrderedError S .AA' .BA'' RA reverse ≤ 4 * eta + 8 * δQ ∧
   187	          extendedPolynomialOrderedError S .BB' .AB'' RB reverse ≤ 4 * eta + 8 * δQ) ∧
   188	        scalarNonlinearMass S .AA' RA ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   189	          2 * (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q ∧
   190	        scalarNonlinearMass S .BB' RB ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   191	          2 * (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q := by
   192	  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, h⟩ := exists_rounded_polynomial_ordered_estimates
   193	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, ?_⟩
   194	  intro P ε δQ δL S points lines delta eta
   195	  obtain ⟨RA, RB, hRA, hRB, horder⟩ := h P ε δQ δL S points lines
   196	  refine ⟨RA, RB, hRA, hRB, horder, ?_, ?_⟩
   197	  · exact (scalarNonlinearMass_le_ordered_error S .AA' .BA'' (by trivial) RA hRA).trans
   198	      (add_le_add
   199	        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (horder false).1 (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)) le_rfl)
   200	  · exact (scalarNonlinearMass_le_ordered_error S .BB' .AB'' (by trivial) RB hRB).trans
   201	      (add_le_add
   202	        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (horder false).2 (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)) le_rfl)
   203	
   204	end ExtendedLineGame

     4	/-!
     5	# Wrong-variable mass of rounded polynomial outcomes
     6	
     7	The two block orders use the actual projected state vectors and the full
     8	ordered-error sum. A common exceptional coefficient controls all outcomes
     9	of the fixed-block measurement before their weights are summed.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1328-1368`,
    14	`eq:qld-g-separable`, `eq:qld-g-48`, `eq:qld-g-2`, and the two wrong-variable
    15	mass bounds. This supports blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`; it does not establish
    16	the subsequent retained overlaps or global polynomial-pair witness.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus PolynomialImageBounds
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	namespace ExtendedLineGame
    29	
    30	/-- Actual mass of scalar-linear outcomes whose second coefficient in the
    31	chosen order depends on the varying block. In order `XZ` this is the coefficient
    32	of beta depending on x; in order `ZX` it is the coefficient of alpha depending
    33	on z. These are the two classes in `eq:qld-g-prime-xpt-bound` and
    34	`eq:qld-g-prime-zpt-bound`, supporting blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    35	def scalarWrongVariableMass {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    36	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
    37	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
    38	    (reverse : Bool) : ℝ := by
    39	  classical
    40	  exact ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g =>
    41	    (∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m)) (PauliScalar P),
    42	      scalarPolynomial P g = MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 +
    43	        MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1) ∧
    44	    ¬ ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g
    45	      (Finsupp.single (if reverse then 0 else 1) 1) reverse = MvPolynomial.C r),
    46	    ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2
    47	
    48	/-- Exact placement and order transport for the common joint scalar sample.
    49	This also transports the retained-overlap calculation in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    50	theorem placed_fiber_orderedIndicator {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    51	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) (reverse : Bool)
    52	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (v : Fin 2 → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
    53	    orderedIndicator
    54	      (S.placedMeasurement p (S.pointMeasExp p.side (if reverse then .Z else .X) x))
    55	      (S.placedMeasurement p (S.pointMeasExp p.side (if reverse then .X else .Z) z))
    56	      (v 0) (v 1) a =
    57	    let y := fiberQuestionEquiv P reverse ((z, x), v)
    58	    S.place p (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
    59	        y.2.1 * ab.1 + y.2.2 * ab.2 = a),
    60	      if reverse then
    61	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z y.1.2).effect ab.2 *
    62	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X y.1.1).effect ab.1
    63	      else
    64	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X y.1.1).effect ab.1 *
    65	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z y.1.2).effect ab.2) := by
    66	  dsimp only
    67	  rw [S.place_finsetSum, Finset.sum_filter]
    68	  simp only [orderedIndicator, ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect]
    69	  cases reverse
    70	  · simp [fiberQuestionEquiv, ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]
    71	  · apply Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.prodComm (PauliScalar P) (PauliScalar P))
    72	    intro ab
    73	    simp [fiberQuestionEquiv, add_comm, ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]
    74	
    75	/-- Both wrong-variable classes are bounded in their appropriate actual
    76	ordered errors, for every pair of opposite placements. The common exceptional
    77	coefficient and both `md` degree bounds are derived internally. Completeness
    78	and normalization retain the full outcome sum, so there is no outcome-count
    79	loss. This is the quantitative concentration step of
    80	`eq:qld-g-prime-xpt-bound` and `eq:qld-g-prime-zpt-bound`, supporting
    81	blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    82	theorem scalarWrongVariableMass_le_ordered_error {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    83	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopposite : p1.IsOpposite p2)
    84	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side))
    85	    (hR : Measurement.IsProjective R) (reverse : Bool) :
    86	    scalarWrongVariableMass S p1 R reverse ≤
    87	      2 * extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R reverse +
    88	        2 * (((P.m * P.d + P.m * P.d + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) := by
    89	  classical
    90	  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun g =>
    91	    (∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m)) (PauliScalar P),
    92	      scalarPolynomial P g = MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 +
    93	        MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1) ∧
    94	    ¬ ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g
    95	      (Finsupp.single (if reverse then 0 else 1) 1) reverse = MvPolynomial.C r)
    96	  let ψ := fun g => applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 (R.effect g)) S.psiHat
    97	  let X := fun x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P => S.placedMeasurement p2
    98	    (S.pointMeasExp p2.side (if reverse then .Z else .X) x)
    99	  let Z := fun z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P => S.placedMeasurement p2
   100	    (S.pointMeasExp p2.side (if reverse then .X else .Z) z)
   101	  let A := fun (z x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (v : Fin 2 → PauliScalar P) g =>
   102	    applyOperatorToState (orderedIndicator (X x) (Z z) (v 0) (v 1)
   103	      (extendedPolynomialRead P (fiberQuestionEquiv P reverse ((z, x), v)) g)) (ψ g)
   104	  let B : ℝ := ((P.m * P.d + P.m * P.d + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q
   105	  have hmass : ∑ g, ‖ψ g‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
   106	    simpa only [ψ, ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect, S.psiHat_norm, one_pow] using
   107	      sum_projective_state_norm_sq (S.placedMeasurement p1 R)

   109	  have hnorm (g) (hg : g ∈ s) :

   187	/-- The actual rounded measurements satisfy both wrong-variable mass bounds,

   196	theorem exists_rounded_polynomial_wrong_variable_mass :
   197	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   198	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε δQ δL : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   199	        (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ) (_lines : ExtendedLinesWitness S points δL),

   201	        (directPassingErrorEnvelope (δQ + δL) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q))
   202	        P.q (2 * P.m + 2) P.d 1
   203	      let eta := delta + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow delta (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
   204	        2 * Real.sqrt (2 * delta)
   205	      ∃ RA : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice),

   208	        (∀ reverse : Bool,
   209	          extendedPolynomialOrderedError S .AA' .BA'' RA reverse ≤ 4 * eta + 8 * δQ ∧
   210	          extendedPolynomialOrderedError S .BB' .AB'' RB reverse ≤ 4 * eta + 8 * δQ) ∧
   211	        scalarNonlinearMass S .AA' RA ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   212	          2 * (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q ∧
   213	        scalarNonlinearMass S .BB' RB ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   214	          2 * (((2 * P.m + 2) * P.d + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q ∧
   215	        (∀ reverse : Bool,
   216	          scalarWrongVariableMass S .AA' RA reverse ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   217	            2 * (((P.m * P.d + P.m * P.d + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) ∧
   218	          scalarWrongVariableMass S .BB' RB reverse ≤ 2 * (4 * eta + 8 * δQ) +
   219	            2 * (((P.m * P.d + P.m * P.d + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q)) := by
   220	  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, h⟩ := exists_rounded_polynomial_scalar_mass
   221	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, ?_⟩
   222	  intro P ε δQ δL S points lines delta eta
   223	  obtain ⟨RA, RB, hRA, hRB, horder, hNA, hNB⟩ := h P ε δQ δL S points lines
   224	  refine ⟨RA, RB, hRA, hRB, horder, hNA, hNB, ?_⟩
   225	  intro reverse
   226	  constructor
   227	  · exact (scalarWrongVariableMass_le_ordered_error S .AA' .BA''
   228	      (by trivial) RA hRA reverse).trans (add_le_add
   229	        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (horder reverse).1 (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)) le_rfl)

   231	      (by trivial) RB hRB reverse).trans (add_le_add

   234	/-- Mass outside the existing bounded polynomial-pair combining image after

   238	def separatedPolynomialMass {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   239	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   240	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) : ℝ := by

   247	private theorem separatedPolynomialMass_le_three_masses {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   248	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   249	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   250	    separatedPolynomialMass S p R ≤ scalarNonlinearMass S p R +
   251	      scalarWrongVariableMass S p R false + scalarWrongVariableMass S p R true := by
   252	  classical
   253	  simp only [separatedPolynomialMass, scalarNonlinearMass, scalarWrongVariableMass,
   254	    Finset.sum_filter, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
   255	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   256	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   257	  intro g _
   258	  by_cases hlin : ∃ r t : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * P.m)) (PauliScalar P),
   259	      scalarPolynomial P g = MvPolynomial.C r * MvPolynomial.X 0 +
   260	        MvPolynomial.C t * MvPolynomial.X 1
   261	  · by_cases hX : ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g (Finsupp.single 0 1) true =
   262	        MvPolynomial.C r
   263	    · by_cases hZ : ∃ r, blockCoefficientPolynomial P g (Finsupp.single 1 1) false =
   264	          MvPolynomial.C r
   265	      · have himage := exists_polyPair_of_scalar_separated P g hlin hX hZ
   266	        simp only [hlin, hX, hZ, not_true_eq_false, and_false, ↓reduceIte, zero_add]
   267	        split_ifs with hout
   268	        · exact le_rfl
   269	        · exact False.elim (hout himage)
   270	      · simp only [hlin, hX, hZ, not_false_eq_true, not_true_eq_false, and_true,
   271	          and_false, ↓reduceIte, zero_add, add_zero]
   272	        split_ifs <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖]
   273	    · simp only [hlin, hX, not_false_eq_true, not_true_eq_false, true_and, ↓reduceIte,
   274	        zero_add]
   275	      split_ifs <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖]
   276	  · simp only [hlin, not_false_eq_true, false_and, ↓reduceIte, add_zero]
   277	    split_ifs <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖]
   278	
   279	/-- The union of the three excluded classes is bounded in the actual two
   280	ordered errors. The image is the existing faithful `combinePoly` encoding
   281	with both components in `Poly P`. This proves concentration only, as in
   282	`eq:qld-g-non-separable`, supporting blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
   283	theorem separatedPolynomialMass_le_ordered_errors {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   284	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopposite : p1.IsOpposite p2)
   285	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side))
   286	    (hR : Measurement.IsProjective R) :
   287	    separatedPolynomialMass S p1 R ≤
   288	      4 * extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R false +
   289	      2 * extendedPolynomialOrderedError S p1 p2 R true +
   290	      (((12 * P.m * P.d + 4 * P.d + 10 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) := by
   291	  have h := separatedPolynomialMass_le_three_masses S p1 R
   292	  have hN := scalarNonlinearMass_le_ordered_error S p1 p2 hopposite R hR
   293	  have hX := scalarWrongVariableMass_le_ordered_error S p1 p2 hopposite R hR true
   294	  have hZ := scalarWrongVariableMass_le_ordered_error S p1 p2 hopposite R hR false
   295	  refine h.trans ((add_le_add (add_le_add hN hZ) hX).trans_eq ?_)
   296	  push_cast
   297	  ring

   299	/-- Both actual rounded measurements concentrate on faithful separated
   300	polynomial pairs, with error `6E + (12md + 4d + 10)/q` and

   302	The point and directly indexed completed-answer line witnesses are precisely

   305	blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`, without claiming the subsequent retained overlaps
   306	or the source global-pair witness. -/
   307	theorem exists_rounded_polynomial_separated_mass :
   308	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   309	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε δQ δL : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

   311	      let delta := deltaLd a b
   312	        (directPassingErrorEnvelope (δQ + δL) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q))
   313	        P.q (2 * P.m + 2) P.d 1
   314	      let eta := delta + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow delta (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
   315	        2 * Real.sqrt (2 * delta)
   316	      ∃ RA : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice),

   325	          (((12 * P.m * P.d + 4 * P.d + 10 : ℕ) : ℝ) / P.q) := by
   326	  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, h⟩ := exists_rounded_polynomial_ordered_estimates
   327	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, ?_⟩
   328	  intro P ε δQ δL S points lines delta eta
   329	  obtain ⟨RA, RB, hRA, hRB, horder⟩ := h P ε δQ δL S points lines

   331	  · have hA := separatedPolynomialMass_le_ordered_errors S .AA' .BA'' (by trivial) RA hRA

    33	/-- The retained diagonal overlap with the actual opposite point measurement. -/
    34	def retainedPointOverlap {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    35	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement)
    36	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side))
    37	    (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=

    43	private theorem retained_mass_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    44	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
    45	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
    46	    (hR : Measurement.IsProjective R) :
    47	    (∑ pair : PolyPair P,
    48	      ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)))
    49	        S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) = 1 - separatedPolynomialMass S p R := by
    50	  classical
    51	  let w := fun g => ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (R.effect g)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2
    52	  have hmass : ∑ g, w g = 1 := by
    53	    simpa only [w, ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect, S.psiHat_norm, one_pow] using
    54	      sum_projective_state_norm_sq (S.placedMeasurement p R)
    55	        (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p R hR) S.psiHat
    56	  have hgood : Finset.univ.image (directCombinedEmbedding P) =
    57	      Finset.univ.filter (fun g => ∃ pair : PolyPair P,
    58	        MvPolynomial.map (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).toRingHom (g (0 : Fin 1)).1 =
    59	          combinePoly pair.1.1 pair.2.1) := by
    60	    ext g
    61	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_filter]
    62	    exact mem_range_directCombinedEmbedding P g
    63	  change (∑ pair, w (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)) = _
    64	  rw [← Finset.sum_image (f := w) (fun a _ b _ h =>
    65	    (directCombinedEmbedding P).injective h), hgood]
    66	  have hsplit := Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not Finset.univ
    67	    (fun g => ∃ pair : PolyPair P,
    68	      MvPolynomial.map (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).toRingHom (g (0 : Fin 1)).1 =

    74	This is the normalized good/bad identity of `eq:qld-s-good-and-bad`; the

    76	theorem retainedPointMismatch_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    77	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopposite : p1.IsOpposite p2)
    78	    (R : DirectPolyMeasTuple P.extendedDirectLd (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p1.side))
    79	    (hR : Measurement.IsProjective R) (W : PauliKind) :
    80	    retainedPointMismatch S p1 p2 R W =
    81	      1 - separatedPolynomialMass S p1 R - retainedPointOverlap S p1 p2 R W := by
    82	  have hpoint (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (pair : PolyPair P) :
    83	      ‖applyOperatorToState
    84	        (1 - S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side W x).effect (evalAt W x pair)))
    85	        (applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 (R.effect (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)))
    86	          S.psiHat)‖ ^ 2 =
    87	      ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p1 (R.effect (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)))
    88	        S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 - stateQForm S.psiHat
    89	          (S.place p1 (R.effect (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)) *
    90	            S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side W x).effect (evalAt W x pair))) := by
    91	    have hM := S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p2 _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ W x)
    92	      (evalAt W x pair)
    93	    have hG := S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p1 R hR (directCombinedEmbedding P pair)
    94	    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect] at hM hG
    95	    have hcomm := S.place_comm p1 p2 hopposite
    96	      (R.effect (directCombinedEmbedding P pair))
    97	      ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side W x).effect (evalAt W x pair))
    98	    rw [MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq]
    99	    change stateQForm _ _ = _
   100	    have hsub (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB))
   101	        (A B : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   102	        stateQForm ψ (A - B) = stateQForm ψ A - stateQForm ψ B := by
   103	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
   104	    rw [hM.one_sub.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, hM.one_sub.isIdempotentElem.eq,
   105	      hsub, stateQForm_one,
   106	      stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj S.psiHat hG hcomm.symm, hcomm]

    39	/-- The sum of the seven potentially rejecting branches of the supplied

    56	        directLdBranchRejectionProbability P.extendedDirectLd (strategy lines)

\section{Key theorem forms}

Throughout, $q = 2^r$ with $r$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
theorem forms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
  \item \textbf{Divisibility-restricted source candidate.}  The source theorem
  form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.  This restriction makes the auxiliary source game defined;
  it does not settle either soundness-import obligation, so this form is not
  established by the present route.
  \item \textbf{Established directly indexed form.}  Quantum
  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; for simultaneity $\kappa$, the error is
  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,\kappa)
  = a(dm'\kappa)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$.  This form is proved by
  applying the low individual degree theorem to a combined strategy at
  dimension $M=m'+\kappa$, with sampling count $N=2560000M^3d$, and then
  recovering the $\kappa$ polynomial coordinates.  The proof verifies the low
  individual degree theorem's condition $400Md \le N$; it does not invoke
  Theorem~4.7 of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} or verify that theorem's distinct
  condition $K \ge 12m'(d+1)$.  Thus it avoids rather than discharges the
  two source-import obligations of Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}.
  For $k=1$, transport to the seed-indexed game is established: the two
  mixed relations compress exactly and the global relation is recovered
  from point agreement on the original Hilbert spaces. The general-$k$
  seed-indexed source theorem remains open.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}

We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
proof, and admissibility are at
\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
There, the combined point measurements
$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
individual degree game with parameters
\[
  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
\]
of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.

The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
$\chi(s)$ with
\[
  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
\]
so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.

Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
the instantiation without addressing the divisibility.  Thus even before the
two soundness-import obligations below are considered, this route can apply to
the polynomial-pair lemma only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
\label{sec:import-obligations}

The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.

\paragraph{The cited test.}
In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
lines measurements, and with each other, up to
$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.

\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this
dependence is now retained in a correlated residue register rather than
averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of
the direct-game transport, but it has not been composed with the distinct
pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.
(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
which the test has no counterpart branch.
Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
own value bound.

\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that

maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there

In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis

on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}

conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the

where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question

\paragraph{Direct index sampling (soundness established).}
For arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the formalization defines the line-point
distribution over $\F_q^{m'}$ by sampling the point, the axis index
$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
$i-1$ coordinates directly.  In the resulting game, line questions carry
the index $i$ (and, for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place
of the seed $s \in \F_q$.  Soundness form~4 is established for this game

combining reduction analysed in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich}.

auxiliary directly indexed game.  Because the proof does not use the
tensor-code import, it leaves both original import obligations open rather
than establishing them.

The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must be proved at the level
of strategies, not merely of question distributions.  An
$\mathsf{ALine}$ question of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0,s)$ and a
